file02LanguageRuntimeUx.role: Live bytes. Every supported programming-language analyzer/tool component supplies the non-system dependencies it requires inside its signed, verified, platform-qualified component closure. The end user does not separately install, select, update, or manage them. No ambient PATH/system-runtime lookup, project package-manager resolution, or implicit download. Manifest declares every bundled runtime/tool byte and exact tree, entrypoint/loader binding, license/notice, SBOM and attestation, supported platform/compatibility matrix, and capability/performance parity evidence. Missing or incompatible closure returns a typed unavailable result with explicit local/offline remediation; never silently substitutes a system tool or weakens semantics. Narrow exception only for a customer-owned external system that cannot lawfully or technically be bundled; explicit product approval; names ownership/trust/network/prerequisites; appears in manifest and doctor output; typed absence/failure; never marketed or silently treated as a supported self-contained language analyzer. TypeScript motivating case: package/provision compatible Node as verified signed bytes and reject ambient/global Node. Quality sentence used only as the G14 limb: the signed closure produces accepted quality on clean offline machines; for TypeScript that includes no ambient/global Node. File 02's Rust-analysis sentence is not a slice-1 role and is not minted here. This specification does not rewrite those bytes.
